item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q001_histone_related_proteins","answer":"In SCOPe, the relationship around canonical histones is the all-alpha Histone-fold fold: class a, fold a.22, superfamily a.22.1. Eukaryotic core histones H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 are close enough to be placed in the core-histone family within that superfamily; archaeal histones are homologous histone-fold proteins but are separated as an archaeal-histone family; and more remote histone-fold transcription/regulatory subunits, such as TFIID TAF histone-fold domains and CCAAT-binding/NF-YB-NF-YC-like histone-fold factors, belong with them at the same histone-fold superfamily/fold level rather than in the eukaryotic core-histone family. The shared SCOPe signal is the three-helix histone-fold dimerization module, so it supports remote structural homology and can be useful for recognizing or modeling that compact helical domain. It should not be used to transfer the full nucleosome core particle role, eukaryotic histone-tail modifications, octamer stoichiometry, or exact DNA-packaging function onto archaeal histones or TAF/NF-Y-like transcription factors without independent functional evidence.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
